next_authority.question: At T8, do temporal shifts continue to decrease and does the R512-R1024 spatial gap stabilize, continue increasing, or reverse relative to T4?

scientific_interpretation: The completed R512/R1024 x T1/T2/T4 matrix shows temporal convergence at both spatial resolutions with similar descriptive order, about 0.65 at R512 and 0.68 at R1024.
Despite decreasing temporal shifts, the matched spatial gap grows monotonically from about 0.01928 cm/d at T1 to 0.02107 at T2 and 0.02233 at T4.
The T2-T4 temporal shift remains subdominant to the T4 spatial gap: about 21% at R512 and 27% at R1024.

The spatial-gap increase therefore is not explained by temporal error simply dominating the comparison. Instead, the matched matrix shows a persistent space-time interaction in which the estimated spatial gap changes as the transaction interval is refined.
A further spatial extension at T1 or T2 would mix unresolved temporal interaction into the spatial inference. The next clean test is matched T8 at both R512 and R1024.
